destinations.name: Altit fort
destinations.description: An ancient fort at Altit town in the Hunza valley in Gilgit Baltistan, Pakistan, it was originally home to the hereditary rulers of the Hunza state.

destinations.name: Amburiq Mosque
destinations.description: Located in Shigar, The Amburiq Mosque is one of the oldest mosques in the region.

destinations.name: Aror
destinations.description: Aror once served as the capital of Sindh. It is mentioned as an important trading center in early Buddhist literature. A massive earthquake that changed the course of the Indus River and ruined the town's mud brick building, thereby setting into play the city's decline.

destinations.name: Attabad Lake
destinations.description: Attabad Lake is in Gojal region of Hunza -a mountainous valley in the northern part of the Gilgit-Baltistan formed by the Hunza River, bordering Afghanistan's Wakhan Corridor to the north and the Xinjiang region of China to the northeast.

destinations.name: Attock Fort
destinations.description: Attock Fort was constructed in 1581 on the orders of the Mughal Emperor Akbar to protect the passage of the River Indus. It is located at a distance of 80 km from the capital city of Islamabad.

destinations.name: Badshahi Mosque
destinations.description: The Badshahi Mosque of Lahore was constructed by the Mughal emperor Aurangzeb between 1671 and 1673 and was the largest mosque in the world from 1673 to 1986.

destinations.name: Bagrote
destinations.description: Bagrote Valley is a valley in the Karakoram Mountain range in the GilgitâBaltistan district of northern Pakistan.

destinations.name: Baha Lake
destinations.description: Baha Lake is also known as Khukush Langar Lake is a colossal lake lying at the feet of transcending mountains.

destinations.name: balochistan
destinations.description: A land that is yet to be explored by travelers around the world. Balochistan has managed to preserve its beauty because it has not been urbanised as much as other areas.

destinations.name: Begum Shahi Mosque
destinations.description: A 17th-century mosque situated in the Walled City of Lahore,built between 1611 and 1614 during the reign of Mughal Emperor Jahangir in honor of his mother. One of the earliest surviving example of a Mughal-era mosque.

destinations.name: Bhangianwali Toap
destinations.description: The cannon was cast in about 1757 in Lahore, now in Pakistan but at the time part of the Durrani Empire. Displayed in front of the Lahore Museum in Lahore, it was one of the largest cannon ever made in the sub-continent.

destinations.name: Bhit Khori
destinations.description: Bhit Khori, one of the finest beaches in Pakistan, asks you to complete a rocky journey before it gifts you with its golden sands and beautiful, cerulean seawater.

destinations.name: Bhodesar Mosque
destinations.description: This mosque with white pillars in Bhodesar is a small marble and limestone structure near the pond embankment is built in 1436 AD. It was built by Mehmood Shah Bin Zaffar Shah, ruler of Gujrat. The mosque is located 5 Km from town Nagarparkar.

destinations.name: Buddhist Stupa Nawabshah
destinations.description: A solid cylindrical structure, tapering at the top, constructed with a brick casing about 60 feet in height stands over a square base about 66 feet in each side. Located in the village of Thul Mir Rukan.

destinations.name: Changa Manga Forest
destinations.description: The Changa Manga is a planted forest which includes a wildlife preserve, in the Kasur and Lahore districts of Punjab. The Changa Manga forest was originally planted in 1866 by British foresters. The forest is home to many species of animals.

destinations.name: Chaukhandi tombs
destinations.description: Chaukhandi Tombs, located about 29 km east of Karachi, Pakistan, are an ancient graveyard dating back to the 15thâ18th centuries. Known for their intricate sandstone carvings and pyramid-like structures, the tombs mostly belong to the Jokhio tribe and other local clans. Carvings on the graves reflect local art, culture, and traditionsâdepicting warriors, jewelry, and symbols of honor. Blending Islamic and Hindu d

destinations.name: Cholistan
destinations.description: The Cholistan Desert, locally known as Rohi, stretches across southern Punjab, Pakistan, extending into Sindh and the Indian Thar Desert. Covering over 26,000â¯kmÂ², it was once a fertile plain nourished by the ancient Hakra (Ghaggar) River. Today it's home to more than 400 Indus Valley Civilization archaeological sites

destinations.name: Delhi Gate
destinations.description: The Delhi Gate was originally built during the Mughal period, served as the main gateway to Lahore, and during the Mughal era its doors were shut every evening. The surrounding area includes several buildings of historical significance near it.

destinations.name: Diran peak
destinations.description: Standing at the height of 7,266 Meters, Diran is a sight to behold. This pyramid shaped mountain is known as the most dangerous mountain of Pakistan due to large snow caps.

destinations.name: Do Darya
destinations.description: With a great atmosphere, multiple cuisine options, and beautiful views, restaurants at Do Darya have quickly garnered a reputation and a loyal customers from all over the city. Nothing can top the experience of the Do Darya food scene.

destinations.name: Dreamworld Resort
destinations.description: At Dreamworld Resort, you along with your family will be able to keep yourself entertained throughout the stay. Providing a serene and tranquil gateway of quality living for the whole family and to rejuvenate ones mind and body.

destinations.name: Eagle Nest View point
destinations.description: Enjoy the best views of Hunza, away from the hustle and bustle of the main valley

destinations.name: Emporium Mall
destinations.description: The most indicatively planned and largest mall in Lahore. This mall is a home to more than 200 brands from local and international chains. Having the largest food court of the city and is dominated with a huge multiplex cinema, banquet halls and supermarket.

destinations.name: Empress Market
destinations.description: Built at the time of Queen Victoria, Empress market considered as the most populous and crowded area of the city. Mass number from all of Karachi come to this place for shopping.

destinations.name: Fairy Meadows
destinations.description: Named by some German climbers and locally known as Jaugth, Fairy Meadows is a grassland near one of Nanga Parbat's base campsites.

destinations.name: Faiz Mahal
destinations.description: A grand architectural masterpiece, unique traditional culture and traditional work of art seems to have swept over the real splendor. Details on the walls of the palace are exquisitely designed, exhibiting the fine art of the people of past era.

destinations.name: Fort Munroe Hill
destinations.description: Fort Munro named after a British administrator, Col Munroe is located in Southern Punjab at the foothills of the Suleiman Range. It attracts a number of tourists every year, particularly those who wish to escape from the hot plains of southern Punjab.

destinations.name: Ganda Singh Wala
destinations.description: Ganda Singh Wala is a village in Kasur, Punjab. A daily 6 p.m Beating Retreat Border Ceremony is jointly held at the border crossing by the military of both nations. The ceremony is attended mostly by local Punjabi's on either side of the border.

destinations.name: gilgit baltistan
destinations.description: Explore the untamed and stunning nature that surrounds Gilgit â from serene meadows, to calming rivers, to imposing mountains and more..

destinations.name: Gilgit Chinese memorial cemetery
destinations.description: The Gilgit Chinese Memorial Cemetery locally known as the China Memorial is a graveyard located in Danyor, GilgitâBaltistan, about ten kilometres away from the capital city of Gilgit across the Gilgit River.

destinations.name: Giri Fort
destinations.description: Giri Fort built in the fifth century perhaps as a stronghold for the thousands of monks in Taxila Valley. Two groups of Buddhist establishments are found here, a fort, a Muslim Ziarat and mosques, all ranging from the early Kushana period to the time of Akbar.

destinations.name: Gorakh Hill
destinations.description: Gorakh Hill is a hill station of Sindh. It is situated on one of the highest plateaus of Sindh, spread over 2,500 acres. The hill station is well known for itâs nightlife, especially for itâs bonfires.

destinations.name: Gori Temple
destinations.description: Despite the effects of fire and gun powder, it is the best surviving temple here, built of local stone with pillars and details of marble from Rajputana. The shrine itself which formerly had a âSikharaâ of typical Kathiawar type is now adorned with rows of miniature âSikharasâ.

destinations.name: Gumti Water Fountain
destinations.description: Gumti Water Fountain is a monument in Faisalabad, Pakistan preserved from the British Raj era. It was a general meeting place of the city folk for local town meetings.

destinations.name: Gurdwara Chakki Sahib Jee
destinations.description: Gurdwara Chakki Sahib Jee, at Eminabad is located where a large millstone chakkis was kept.

destinations.name: Gurdwara Chowa Sahib
destinations.description: Gurdwara Chowa Sahib is an abandoned gurdwara, located at the northern edge of the Rohtas Fort, near Jhelum, Punjab. The current building dates from 1834, and was commissioned by Maharaja Ranjit Singh.

destinations.name: Gurdwara Darbar Sahib Kartarpur
destinations.description: Gurdwara Darbar Sahib Kartarpur, also called Kartarpur Sahib, built on the historic site where the founder of Sikhism, Guru Nanak, settled and assembled the Sikh community. Notable for its location near the border between Pakistan and India.

destinations.name: Gurdwara Dera Sahib
destinations.description: A Sikh temple in Lahore which commemorates the spot where the 5th guru of Sikhism was martyred in 1606. The gurdwara is located just outside of the Walled City of Lahore and is part of an ensemble of monuments.

destinations.name: Gurdwara Janam Asthan Guru Ram Das Jee
Gurdwara Panja Sahib
destinations.description: Gurdwara Panja Sahib Jee is a famous gurdwara located near Islamabad, Hasan Abdal.

destinations.name: Gurdwara Sachi Sauda
destinations.description: Gudwara sacha sauda is situated in Farooqabad, Sheikhupura Punjab. Guru Nanak as a young man was sent by his father Mehta Kalu to instill a sense of business in his son.

destinations.name: Hafeez Jalandhari Tomb
destinations.description: Hafeez Jalandhari was a Pakistani Urdu-language poet who wrote the lyrics for the National Anthem of Pakistan. Buried in Model Town, Lahore later shifted to a tomb built by the Government of Pakistan near Minar-e-Pakistan in Lahore, the site of Pakistan Resolution.

destinations.name: Haram of Talpur Mirs
destinations.description: Mir Haram is another simple but impressive building situated inside the Pucca Fort, The interior of the Haram is profusely decorated with fresco paintings, though of degenerated quality.

destinations.name: Harappa
destinations.description: Harappa is a large village, presently in the province of Punjab. The modern town is a part of and lies next to the ancient city. The site of the ancient city contains the ruins of a Bronze Age fortified city.

destinations.name: Harappa
destinations.description: Harappa is a large village, presently in the province of Punjab. The modern town is a part of and lies next to the ancient city. The site of the ancient city contains the ruins of a Bronze Age fortified city.

destinations.name: Haveli Barood Khana
destinations.description: Built in the 18th century by a Sikh commanding general and used as a house. Considering the hot temperature of Lahore, the haveli has high ceilings. The room also has murals of the Sikh general fighting demons.

destinations.name: Haveli of Nau Nihal Singh
destinations.description: The haveli is considered to be one of the finest examples of Sikh architecture in Lahore preserved in its original architecture.

destinations.name: Hingol National Park,Balochistan
destinations.description: Hingol National Park is the largest national park in Pakistan and is named after the southern part of the Hangul River which flows along the shores of the Arabian Sea and is home to large numbers of waterfowl and marine life.

destinations.name: Hunza Valley
destinations.description: Hunza is a mountainous valley in the northern part of the Gilgit-Baltistan formed by the Hunza River, bordering Afghanistan's Wakhan Corridor to the north and the Xinjiang region of China to the northeast.

destinations.name: Hushe Valley
destinations.description: Hushe Valley is a valley in Ghanche District, Gilgit-Baltistan, Pakistan. Created by the Hushe River, the valley runs from Masherbrum Mountain (at 7,821 meters) and close by glaciers south to the Shyok River, inverse Khaplu.

destinations.name: hyderabad
destinations.description: Hyderabad, the Lion's City, with its historical architecture, rich history, and scrumptious Sindhi cuisine is one of the best go-to cities in Sindh.

destinations.name: Ishkoman
destinations.description: The Ishkoman valley lies in the north of Ghizer District in Gilgit-Baltistan, Pakistan, lining Afghanistan and the Pamir Wakhan Corridor.

destinations.name: Jain Temple
destinations.description: The temple is made of stone and consists of an open group of pillars with carved capitals. From this temple was found a beautifully carved block of marble which is now on display in the National Museum of Pakistan, Karachi.

destinations.name: Jamia Mosque Bhong
destinations.description: Bhong Mosque is located in the village of Bhong, Rahim Yar Khan District, Punjab Province. It was designed and constructed over a period of nearly 50 years.

destinations.name: Jaulian Buddhist Monastery
destinations.description: Dating from the 2nd century CE, Jaulian monastery along with the nearby monastery at Mohra Muradu, form part of the Ruins of Taxila. Consists of a main central stupa, 27 peripheral smaller stupas, 59 small chapels displaying scenes from the life of Buddha.

destinations.name: Jiwani Coastal Wetland
destinations.description: Jiwani is a town and commercial port that is located along the Gulf of Oman in the Gawadar District of the Balochistan province in Pakistan.

destinations.name: K2
destinations.description: The legendary K2 is the second highest mountain in the world. It is located in the north-western Karakoram Mountain Range on the PakistanâChina border

destinations.name: Kai Valley
destinations.description: Kai Valley presents a picturesque panorama on both sides of the road. Kai Valley is one of the rare solitary landscapes which sees the majority of tourists. It gives the impression as if the hills were once underneath sea.

destinations.name: Kallar Kahar
destinations.description: Alluring scenic beauty, with a calm lake, and breathtaking views, where you can go for cliff-diving, paragliding and many more activities.

destinations.name: Karachi: The City of lights
destinations.description: Karachi is the largest city of Pakistan. With its dazzling bazaars, high-end shopping malls, amazing sightseeing options, and a mix of all cultures, it is surely a must-visit.

destinations.name: Karakoram Mountains
destinations.description: The Karakoram is a mountain range spanning the borders of China, India, and Pakistan. The mountain range is a great challenge for the mountaineers & climbers the world over.

destinations.name: Karambar Lake
destinations.description: Karambar Lake, renowned as Qurumbar Lake, is a high height lake situated in the Ishkoman Valley bilanz in Ghizer District, Gilgit Baltistan, Pakistan.

destinations.name: Kargah Buddha
destinations.description: About 9.7km away from Gilgit, this carved image is part of an archaeological site which stands 50 feet high.

destinations.name: Karimabad
destinations.description: Karimabad, previously known as Baltit, is named after Prince Karim Aga Khan IV. It is the capital of Hunza District, in the Gilgit-Baltistan area of Pakistan.

destinations.name: Kasur
destinations.description: Kasur also Romanized as QasÅ«r is a city to south of Lahore, in the Pakistani province of Punjab. It is also known for being the burial place of the 17th-century Sufi-poet Bulleh Shah. Kasur derives its name from the Arabic word qasur meaning âpalaces,â or âfortsâ.

destinations.name: Katpana Desert
destinations.description: Katpana desert is one of its kind. Being one of the highest deserts, its temperature varies from 27 Â°C in summers to snow covered sand in winters.

destinations.name: Keenjhar Lake Resort
destinations.description: The resort is developed on the bank of Keenjhar lake, which is a favorable and ideal place for winter migratory birds that come from regions of North Asia in the winter season. Located in the center of Thatta district, which has important tourist sites belonging to the near and far past of history.

destinations.name: Khaliq Dina Hall
destinations.description: Khaliq Dina Hall is a library and hall located in Karachi, Pakistan built in 1906. Currently used for various events, a library, and a room that serves as the office of a local NGO.

destinations.name: Khalti Lake
destinations.description: Khalti Lake is located at Gupis-Yasin District, the westernmost piece of the GilgitâBaltistan locale and northernmost domain of Pakistan.

destinations.name: Khaplu Palace
destinations.description: Khaplu Palace is also known as Yabgo Khar (meaning "The fort of Doqsa"), is an old fort located in Khaplu, within the Gilgit-Baltistan region of Pakistan.

destinations.name: Khaplu Valley
destinations.description: Khaplu is a city that serves as the managerial capital of the Ghanche District of Gilgit-Baltistan, in northern Pakistan.

destinations.name: Kharpocho Skardu Fort
destinations.description: The Skardu fort also known as called kharapocho is a stunning and historically significant fort of the Baltistan area.

destinations.name: Khewra Salt Mine
destinations.description: The Khewra Salt Mine is in Khewra, Punjab. Famous for itâs production of pink Khewra salt, often marketed as Himalayan salt, and is a major tourist attraction, drawing thousands of visitors a year.

destinations.name: Khunjerab
destinations.description: A gateway between two great allies , the incredible altitude makes for a very memorable, albeit chilly, experience, which has captured the imaginations of the local people.

destinations.name: Khunjerab National Park
destinations.description: Khunjerab National Park is Pakistan's third largest national park. The park is adjacent to the Taxkorgan Natural Reserve in China. The primary purpose of setting up this park was to provide protection to the endangered Marco polo sheep, which is only found in this area in Pakistan.

destinations.name: Kotdiji Fort
destinations.description: This magnificent fort made from kiln baked bricks sits atop a high semi-circular lime stone hillock. Fifty strategically erected bastions for cannons and to keep a vigilant eye over enemy movement. Its beautifully carved arches & the platform attract the visitors eye immediately.

destinations.name: Kund Malir Beach
destinations.description: Kund Malir beach with its sparkling cerulean waters, beckons visitors to spend the day picnicking or the night camping on its peaceful shore. Add a to that bonfire as the Milky Way unfolds above and it makes for the perfect weekend getaway.

destinations.name: Lahoot Lamakan
destinations.description: Lahoot Lamakan is a cave in Balochistan, Pakistan. The water flows from the external limestone shell of the cave and believers have a tale that first it was milk when people began to sell it, miraculously it became water.

destinations.name: Lahore
destinations.description: A city where history, culture, and hospitality come alive. Explore its grand Mughal monuments, vibrant bazaars, rich cuisine, and lively streets that never sleep.

destinations.name: Lahore Fort Food Street
destinations.description: Travelers from all across the world come to feast on some of the most delicious desi food. Offering enchanting views of Badshahi Mosque and Lahore Fort, the delicious food is bound to make your visit to this food street unforgettable.

destinations.name: Lansdowne Bridge
destinations.description: The Lansdowne Bridge is a 19th-century bridge that spans the Indus River between the cities of Sukkur and Rohri, in Sindh.

destinations.name: Leepa Valley
destinations.description: Leepa Valley is located in Hattian Bala District of Azad Kashmir. With fields of rice apple found all over the valley, its lush green river fields in summer and typical wooden kashmiri houses present a wonderful view to the tourists.

destinations.name: Madyan
destinations.description: Madyan presents dense, lush greenery under a clear, blue sky. With the rivers and streams that accent the scenery on occasion making one feel closer to nature.

destinations.name: Makli Necropolis
destinations.description: Makli Necropolis near Thatta is one of the worldâs largest graveyards, home to stunning tombs and mausoleums from the 14th to 18th century. Its rich history and intricate art make it a remarkable heritage site.

destinations.name: Malot Temples
destinations.description: Malot Hindu Temples are located in the Salt Range of Pakistan near the city of Kallar Kahar. A serene place where the cliffs by the temple present a beautiful panoramic view.

destinations.name: Mankiala Stupa
destinations.description: A 2nd-century Buddhist stupa near the village of Tope Mankiala, built to commemorate the spot, where according to the Jataka tales, an incarnation of the Buddha called Prince Sattva sacrificed himself to feed seven hungry tiger cubs.

destinations.name: Manora Beach
destinations.description: The long sandy beaches along the southern edge of the Manora Island are popular as Manora beach that is serving tourists as a popular picnic spot due to its incredible geographical location.

destinations.name: Manthal Buddha Rock
destinations.description: Manthal Buddha Rock refers to a giant granite rock on which an image of Buddha has incised that in all probability dates back to the eighth century.

destinations.name: Masherbrum
destinations.description: Masherbrum, formerly known as K1 is located in the Ghanche District, Gilgit Baltistan. At 25,659 feet, it is the 22nd highest mountain in the world. The mighty Masherbrum Peaks in Pakistan are perfect for every tough mountaineer to prepare themselves for higher altitude peaks.

destinations.name: Meeran Ja Qubba
destinations.description: The tombs of Talpur Mirs have been built since the British conquest. From an architectural point of view they are conspicuously inferior to those of Kalhoras. For some time these tombs were maintained by their families.

destinations.name: Mirs Tombs, Khairpur
destinations.description: Khairpur, in northern Sindh, was once the capital of the Talpur princely state. Known for its royal heritage, Faiz Mahal, historic forts, Sufi shrines, handicrafts, and lush date orchards, it offers a rich blend of history, culture, and rural charm for heritage and spiritual tourism.

destinations.name: Mirza Jani Baig Tarkhan's Tomb
destinations.description: The mausoleum of Mirza Jani Baig Tarkhan presents a picturesque and colourful sight. The brick masonry, in alternate courses of glazed dark-blue and unglazed red bricks, represents a high standard of Sindhi craftsmanship.

destinations.name: Mohatta Palace Museum
destinations.description: The Mohatta Palace Museum offers a diverse range of activities for both the casual and informed visitor. Families and school children are particularly welcome and tours can be arranged in advance.

destinations.name: Mohenjo-daro
destinations.description: Mohenjo-daro, built around 2500 BCE near Larkana, Sindh, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and a marvel of the ancient Indus Valley Civilization. Its planned streets and smart drainage reflect a highly advanced urban life.

destinations.name: Monument of Van Alexander Agnew
destinations.description: This monument was erected by the British East India Company in honor of Patrick Alexander Vans Agnew and Lieutenant W. A. Anderson.

destinations.name: Moti Mosque
destinations.description: Moti Masjid is a 17th-century religious building located inside the Lahore Fort, Lahore, and Punjab, Pakistan. It is a small, white marble structure built by Mughal emperor Jahangir.

destinations.name: Mubarak Village Beach
destinations.description: The crystal clear greenish-blue waters and unspoiled coastline have made this spot gain immense popularity in recent years. One can indulge in all sorts of water sports on the trip to Mubarak Village, including boating, beaching, snorkeling, and scuba diving.

destinations.name: Multan Fort
destinations.description: A military installation built between 800 and 1000 B.C. The fort originally known as Katochgarh and is attributed to have been built by the Katoch Dynasty was notable for both its effectiveness as a defense installation and for its architecture.

destinations.name: Nagar
destinations.description: In an eponymous valley with splendid scenery, Nagar is a small town. A visit during the right season, you can see trees of many different colors with lakes, rivers, and clear skies abound.

destinations.name: NagarParkar
destinations.description: Nagarparkar, near the PakistanâIndia border, lies at the foot of the Karoonjhar Hills and is known for its desert scenery, granite outcrops, and rich cultural heritage. Home to ancient Jain temples, Hindu shrines, and the historic Bhodesar Mosque, it offers a unique blend of history, spirituality, and Thari cultureâespecially vibrant during the monsoon season.

destinations.name: Naltar Valley
destinations.description: renowned for its lakes whose waters change colours depending on the time of day. The three lakes are known by several names. According to locals, one of the lakes is called the Pari Lake because of its enchanting, deep blue colour.

destinations.name: Nankana Sahib
destinations.description: A small town in Punjab thatâs one of the most sacred locations for Sikhs. The town boasts a beautiful gurdwara with marvelous architecture, which has the power to inspire and amaze.

destinations.name: Nathia Gali
destinations.description: Ideal for hiking, trekking and sightseeing, with its crowning jewel, Mushkpuri peak, Nathia Gali is the place to experience nature's true beauty.

destinations.name: National Museum of Pakistan
destinations.description: The National Museum of Pakistan established in Frere Hall on 17 April 1950. In 1950 with a primary duty to counsel the Museum on the issues of enriching its collection through new acquisitions and purchase of antiquities and works of Arts. The Museum was shifted in Burns Garden in 1970.

destinations.name: Naukot Fort
destinations.description: The fort was used by Talpur Mirs as a strong hold cum-residence. Most probably these buildings were used as residences and a few of them for imprisoning the prisoners.

destinations.name: Neela Sandh Waterfall
destinations.description: Neela Sandh is a delightful waterfall, situated in Mori Syedan, Rawalpindi, Punjab. It has numerous greenery, tall trees and extensive mountains which are relatively secured with snow constantly. Guests who adore swimming unquestionably visit to enjoy with their families and companions.

destinations.name: Neelum Valley
destinations.description: The valley is situated in the northeast of Muzaffarabad, running parallel to Kaghan Valley. It is replete with gorgeous scenery, stunning valleys, and magical waterfalls.

destinations.name: Nigar Khana
destinations.description: Nigar Khana known as a House of Art for selling handicrafts, exhibits antiquities, cultural and artistic items for over 45 years. one finds oneself into a world of colors consisted of mosaic art, Naqashi, wooden, glass work etc.

destinations.name: Noor Mahal
destinations.description: Bahawalpur, due to the lack of publicity.

destinations.name: Old Jamia Masjid Thatta
destinations.description: The large brick masonry structure, built by Samma ruler Jam Tamachi, as homage to the Sufi saint. The masonry walls are in a highly degraded state with a collapsed roof showing its age.

destinations.name: Passu Cones
destinations.description: Breathtaking views of majestic Passu Cones (few pointed cone-like snow covered peaks) are in the Karakorum Range in north of the Gulmit village in Gojal Valley.

destinations.name: Phander Valley
destinations.description: Phander is the name of a settlement and valley in the Gupis-Yasin District of Pakistan's reliant region of Gilgit-Baltistan.

destinations.name: Pharwala Fort
destinations.description: Pharwala Fort is a 15th-century fort built by the Gakhars located in Rawalpindi. The fort is naturally defended on one side by a small Himalayan range and the other by the Soan River.

destinations.name: Pindi Food Street
destinations.description: A must visit place for the food lovers, if one is visiting Rawalpindi. There are a variety of restaurants and food to enjoy with family and friends.

destinations.name: Princess of Hope
destinations.description: The Princess of Hope is a natural rock formation that manifests a princess looking beyond the horizon. The site is located in the Hingol National Park in the Lasbela District of Balochistan.

destinations.name: punjab
destinations.description: Punjab, âThe Land of Five Riversâ, is a culturally and historically rich province, with extra-ordinary landscape.

destinations.name: Quetta
destinations.description: The city is known as the "Fruit Garden of Pakistan," due to the numerous fruit orchards in and around it, and the large variety of fruits and dried fruit products produced there.

destinations.name: Qutb-ud-Din Aibak's Tomb
destinations.description: The tomb was built, in its present form, during the 1970s by the Department of Archaeology and Museums which tried to emulate the Sultanate-era architecture. Prior to the modern construction, the Sultan's grave existed in a simple form and was enclosed by residential houses.

destinations.name: Raja Bazaar
destinations.description: Oldest place in Rawalpindi present in the heart of the city. All sorts of things are available for customers at a reasonable price, from retailers to wholesale are present. Crowded by people surfing their time in shopping.

destinations.name: Rakaposhi
destinations.description: Part of the Karakoram range, Rakaposhi is the 27th highest mountain in the world. The mountain resides in the middle of the Bagrote valley, danyor and Nagar Valley.

destinations.name: Reko Diq Mine
destinations.description: The Reko Diq Mine is located near Reko Diq town, Balochistan. Reko Diq represents one of the largest copper and gold reserves in the world having estimated reserves of 5.9 billion tonnes of ore.

destinations.name: Rock carvings at Thalpan
destinations.description: Located at the mid-point between Islamabad and Gilgit-Skardu, the rock carvings at Thalpan are in Chilas Valley, Gilgit

destinations.name: Rohtas Fort
destinations.description: Pashtun King Sher Shah Suri, the founder of short-lived Suri dynasty, built the Rohtas Fort in the 16th century. It is located near the city of Jhelum.

destinations.name: Rush Lake
destinations.description: Rush Lake is a high-altitude lake situated in Nagar Valley, Gilgit-Baltistan, Pakistan close to Rush Pari Peak. At 4,694 meters (15,400 ft), Rush is one of the most elevated high lakes on the planet.

destinations.name: Sadh Belo
destinations.description: An island on Indus River very close to the city of Sukkur, There is a Hindu temple on the island which was founded in 1823 by Swami Bakhandi Maharaj Udasi. Provides the tourist with a pleasurable experience and scenic view of River Indus.

destinations.name: Sadhu da Bagh caves
destinations.description: The village is believed to be more than seven hundred years old. Relics of the Buddhist era, dating back to the 8th century can be found here.
